given.why: Two loans are lent through POST /loans and never returned, so both are open when the job runs.
The loans fall due on 2026-03-16 and the clock is set to 2026-03-17, the day after; B2's not-yet-overdue loan covers the other side of that line.
The clock is always set to 10:00Z, so code that worked out today in local time would get the same date in nearly every timezone and still pass.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The only case set up is a loan with no reminders at all; no loan was reminded on an earlier day, so code that skips any loan ever reminded (not just reminded today) would pass both B1 and B2.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: The fake's `sent` list must hold exactly two entries, each with the right member, loanId and dueOn, so skipping the call or sending to the wrong memberId fails.
The reminders table must hold exactly one row for each loan.
`sent_on` must be 2026-03-17, the clock's date, which is not the dueOn of 2026-03-16.
B3: if the code recorded before asking, the refused loan would get a reminder row, and B3's exact check of the reminders table would fail.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so on the second run loan1 already has a reminder recorded today.
loan2 is overdue but is returned before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 03-03, so it falls due on 03-17, which is today; that tests the boundary.

then.why: When `toMatchObject` is given an array it also checks the length, so a second send for loan1, or any send for loan2 or loan3, makes `sent` too long and the test fails.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with the reason "Notifications API answered 503".
B5: the client turns a failed connection into a refusal, so from the job's side it is the same refused case B3 sets up.

then.why: The reminders table must contain only loan2's row.
`toContainEqual` checks the event name exactly.
The log level must be exactly `warn`.
The `loanId` field must equal loan1's ID, so logging the memberId instead fails.
`error` must equal the exact reason the fake refused with.

then.part: and carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 falls due after loan1 and must still be sent, so stopping at loan1's refusal fails; this relies on the job taking loan1 first.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans, one of them refused, are all handled in a single run.

then.why: The last log entry must equal this event exactly.
The log level must be exactly `info`.
`sent` must be 2.
`failed` must be 1.

given.why: A real reminder is built and handed to the real client in every test.

then.why: The recorded method must be exactly POST, and the handler only matches POST.
The path must be /notifications, the handler only matches on NOTIFY_URL, and any other request is set to fail the test (onUnhandledRequest: "error").
The content-type must be exactly `application/json`, and the body is read as JSON.
The whole body is compared with `toEqual`, so a renamed key or a wrong value fails.
The template value is compared exactly.
The `data` object must equal exactly loanId and dueOn.
200, 202 and 204 must each come back as accepted, so a check for exactly 200 fails.

then.part: any other answer counts as refused
then.why: Only a 400 is tried; code that refused only on 4xx, or that let 3xx through, would pass because no 5xx or 3xx answer is ever set up.

then.part: a failed connection counts as refused
then.why: `HttpResponse.error()` must come back as `{ kind: "refused" }`, not as a thrown error.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain "400", so a fixed message fails; only the 400 case is checked, though.

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain "unreachable".
